passage: In the fest committee's room, Seema noticed that Vasudha had sighed four times in an hour. Vasudha had sent the wrong date to the sponsors, misspelled a name on the banner and now sat with a packed lunchbox untouched beside the laptop. Seema thought about telling Vasudha to “take it easy” and “make a schedule”, and then dropped the idea; it would only be one more thing to carry. Instead she pulled a chair over and asked, “What can I take off your plate this week?” Vasudha stared, then laughed weakly. “The sponsor emails. Can you do those?” Seema nodded and drafted the first one right there while Vasudha finally opened the lunchbox.

qa.q: How many times did Vasudha sigh in an hour?
qa.a: Vasudha sighed four times in an hour.

qa.q: Why did Seema drop the idea of telling Vasudha to take it easy?
qa.a: Seema felt concerned for Vasudha and wary of adding to the load, sensing that such advice would only be one more thing for Vasudha to carry.

qa.q: What did Seema do that helped?
qa.a: Seema asked what could be taken off Vasudha's plate, then drafted the first sponsor email so Vasudha could eat lunch.

qa.q: What might Vasudha be feeling when staring and then laughing weakly?
qa.a: Vasudha is probably overwhelmed and relieved at being asked, and the weak laugh shows exhaustion and a little gratitude.

grounding: A peer notices someone missing details, sighing and skipping lunch, and offers to take something off their plate.

“You haven't touched your lunch again,” Akash said quietly. He was in the intern room, and Mahima was hunched at the next screen.
“I'm not hungry. I need to finish this before four.”
“You sent the wrong file to the client twice today. That's not like you.”
Mahima rubbed her eyes. “I know. I've got three reports and the training deck and Ma's been calling about the wedding tickets.”
“I won't tell you how to organise it,” said Akash. “What could I take off your plate?”
A pause. “The training deck?”
“Send me the folder.”
Mahima's shoulders came down for the first time that day.

qa.q: How many times had Mahima sent the wrong file to the client?
qa.a: Mahima had sent the wrong file to the client twice today.

qa.q: What might Akash be thinking when he says, "That's not like you"?
qa.a: Akash is concerned and caring: noticing the untouched lunch and the two wrong files, Akash worries about Mahima and wants to help without lecturing.

qa.q: What did Akash choose to ask instead of giving advice?
qa.a: Akash asked what he could take off Mahima's plate, and took the training deck.

qa.q: What is it like for Mahima before Akash speaks?
qa.a: Mahima is stretched thin and tense, with three reports, a deck and calls about the wedding tickets, and relief shows in the shoulders coming down once someone offers to take a task.

grounding: A peer notices someone missing details and skipping lunch, and asks what could be taken off their plate.

passage: I'm Indu, and I share a lab bench with Binita in our second-year biotech course. Last month I started noticing things. Binita, who never makes mistakes, mislabelled two test tubes. She sighed every few minutes, a long tired sound. She skipped lunch three days in a row, saying she had to finish something. One afternoon her phone buzzed with a message from her tuition student's mother, then her hostel warden, then her project partner. I wanted to tell her to sleep more, or make a schedule. I didn't. I asked, "Is there anything I could take off your plate this week?" She stared at me, then laughed shakily. "Could you write up the lab report?"

qa.q: How many days in a row did Binita skip lunch?
qa.a: Binita skipped lunch three days in a row.

qa.q: What was Indu feeling while noticing the changes in Binita?
qa.a: Indu felt concerned and uneasy, seeing someone who never made mistakes mislabelling test tubes and sighing constantly.

qa.q: Why was Indu's question better than advice?
qa.a: Asking what could be taken off Binita's plate offered real relief, while advice about sleep or schedules would have added one more demand.

qa.q: How might Binita feel when Indu asks the question?
qa.a: Binita seems surprised and relieved, laughing shakily and quickly naming something Indu could take.

grounding: A peer notices someone missing details, sighing and skipping lunch, and asks what could be taken off her plate.

passage:
Teaching assistant's note, chemistry lab, Week 9.
I have noticed a change in Jaya, a second-year student. She has forgotten to record data twice this week, which is unlike her careful work earlier in the term. She sighs often and I saw her skip the lunch break to finish another course's worksheet. She mentioned a part-time job and a family function. I did not want to lecture her about time management; I think she knows. Instead I asked, "Is there something here I can take off your plate?" She asked if the lab report deadline could move by three days. I agreed and informed the professor, Ujjwal sir. I will check in with Jaya next week.

qa.q: How many times did Jaya forget to record data this week?
qa.a: She forgot to record data twice this week.

qa.q: How does the teaching assistant seem to feel about Jaya?
qa.a: The teaching assistant seems concerned and caring, noticing the change and choosing not to lecture.

qa.q: What did the teaching assistant do, and why did it help?
qa.a: They asked what could be taken off Jaya's plate and moved the lab report deadline by three days, easing one real demand.

qa.q: How might Jaya feel when the deadline is moved?
qa.a: Jaya would likely feel relieved and grateful, with one less thing pressing on an overloaded week.

grounding: A teaching assistant observes signs of overload in a student and asks what can be taken off her plate instead of giving advice.

passage:
Dear Diary, Thursday
Simran looked terrible today. We work the same shift at the college café, and she forgot two orders, which she never does. She kept sighing, and when I offered her a samosa at lunch she said she had no time to eat. She's doing her final-year project, tutoring two kids and looking after her grandmother at home.
I almost said, "You should make a timetable." Then I remembered how I felt when people told me that in first year. So instead I asked if I could take her Saturday shift. She blinked and said, "Really?" Her whole face softened. I'll cover it. My Saturday was free anyway.
Yusuf

qa.q: How many orders did Simran forget?
qa.a: Simran forgot two orders.

qa.q: What was Yusuf feeling when about to give advice?
qa.a: Yusuf felt a pang of recognition, remembering how it felt to be told to make a timetable in first year, and chose not to.

qa.q: What was helpful about Yusuf's offer?
qa.a: Taking Simran's Saturday shift removed a real demand from her week, instead of adding advice.

qa.q: What was it like for Simran when Yusuf offered to take the shift?
qa.a: Simran seemed surprised and relieved, her whole face softening.

grounding: A diary shows a peer noticing signs of overload in a coworker and offering to take something off her plate.
